intro: Short two-verb phrases for «I have just», «again», «start», «stop», «keep on», «about to» and «usually».
p.acabo de.consejo: It goes with an infinitive: «acabo de llegar» means I arrived a very short time ago.
p.vuelvo a.consejo: It goes with an infinitive: «vuelvo a llamar» is «I call again». In «vuelvo», the o becomes «ue».
p.empiezo a.consejo: It goes with an infinitive: «empiezo a entender». The e becomes «ie»: empiezo, empiezas. The z sounds «th».
p.dejo de.consejo: It goes with an infinitive and says something ends: «deja de llover».
p.sigo.consejo: It goes with a gerund: «sigo estudiando». From «seguir»: e becomes i: sigo, sigues, sigue.
p.estoy a punto de.consejo: It goes with an infinitive and says something will happen right away: «el autobús está a punto de salir».
p.suelo.consejo: It goes with an infinitive and speaks of habits: «suelo cenar tarde». The o becomes «ue»: suelo, sueles.
p.llegar.consejo: It is written with «ll», not «y». With «a» it gives the destination: «llegar a casa».
p.llover.consejo: The o becomes «ue»: «llueve». It is used only in the third person: «llueve», «llovía».
p.cenar.consejo: Cenar is to eat at night. The «ce» sounds «the»: the-NAR.
p.el autobús.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable: au-to-BÚS. Plural: «los autobuses», with no accent.
p.a pie.consejo: It is used with no article: «voy a pie». It means to go walking.
b1.texto:
In these phrases, the **first verb** is conjugated and the **second** stays in the infinitive or the gerund.

- **acabar de** + infinitive = «have just»: **acabo de** llegar.
- **volver a** + infinitive = «again»: **vuelve a** llover.
- **empezar a** + infinitive = «start»: **empieza a** llover.
- **dejar de** + infinitive = «stop»: **deja de** llover.
- **estar a punto de** + infinitive = «about to»: **está a punto de** salir.
- **seguir** + gerund = «keep on»: **sigue** lloviendo.
- **soler** + infinitive = «usually»: **suelo** cenar tarde.

Pronouns can go before the first verb or attached to the second: **lo** acabo de ver = acabo de ver**lo**.
b2.f6.texto: The bus is about to leave.
b4.texto:
- **acabar de + infinitive**: Acabo de comer. (a moment ago)
- **volver a + infinitive**: Vuelve a llamar. (again)
- **empezar a + infinitive**: Empiezo a entender. (I begin)
- **dejar de + infinitive**: Deja de llover. (it ends)
- **estar a punto de + infinitive**: Está a punto de salir. (almost now)
- **seguir + gerund**: Sigue lloviendo. (it continues)
- **soler + infinitive**: Suelo leer por la noche. (habit)

The infinitive ends in -ar, -er or -ir. The gerund, in -ando or -iendo.
b4.e1.texto: It is still raining in the street.
b5.f0.texto: The rain has just stopped over the grey city.
b5.f1.texto: The drops keep falling from the wet leaves.
b5.f2.texto: At the stop, an elderly woman begins to fold her umbrella.
b5.f3.texto: A small boy stops crying when he sees the blue sky.
b5.f4.texto: The wind usually brings a smell of wet earth at this time.
b5.f5.texto: The blue bus is about to reach the corner.
b5.f6.texto: All the passengers look at the clock again.
b5.f7.texto: A tall man has just closed his book and puts it in his bag.
b5.f8.texto: The bus door opens with a long sigh.
b5.f9.texto: Little by little, the street goes quiet again.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Dejo de comer» means I stop eating.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Vuelvo a comer» takes «a» and means again.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is it! «Seguir» + gerund is to continue.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is the beginning; «sigue» means it was already raining.
b8.frase: El autobús está a punto de salir
b8.traduccion: The bus is about to leave
b9.o0.refuerzo: With «seguir» you need the gerund, not the infinitive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! «Seguir» goes with a gerund.
b10.pregunta: Write with «soler»: «I usually have dinner late.»
b11.o0.refuerzo: That is the beginning, not the repetition.
b11.pregunta: Which sentence says it rains again?
b12.o1.refuerzo: «De» goes with «dejar» and «acabar»: dejar de, acabar de.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Que» is not used between these two verbs.
p.siguen.consejo: From «seguir», to follow or continue. The gu before e sounds like «g».
p.cayendo.consejo: From «caer», to fall. The -endo ending means «in the middle of».
p.traer.consejo: The stress is on the last syllable. The e and r are both clear.
p.pasajeros.consejo: The j sounds like h. The stress is on HE.
p.acabo.consejo: From «acabar», to finish. The -o ending means «I».
